# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 78 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 78 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_078_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 1

**1** He showed me a great willow tree whose shade spread over plains and mountains, and under its shade had gathered all those who are called by the name of the Lord. **2** Standing beside the willow was a glorious and very tall angel of the Lord, holding a great sickle; he was cutting branches from the willow and giving them to the people sheltered under the willow — a small rod to each, about a cubit in length. **3** After all had received their rods, the angel laid down his sickle, and the tree was intact, just as I had seen it before. **4** I marveled inwardly: "How can the tree be sound after so many branches were cut from it?" The Shepherd said to me, "Do not marvel that the tree has remained sound after having so many branches cut off. Wait until you have seen everything, and it will be shown to you what this means." **5** The angel who had given the rods to the people then asked them back; and they were summoned to him in the same order in which each had received a rod, and each returned his rod. The angel of the Lord took them and examined them. **6** From some he received rods that were withered and moth-eaten; the angel commanded those who had returned rods in that state to stand apart. **7** Others returned their rods withered but not moth-eaten; these also were commanded to stand apart. **8** Others returned their rods half-withered; these also stood apart. **9** Others returned rods half-withered and cracked; these too stood apart. **10** Others returned rods that were green but cracked; these also stood apart. **11** Others returned rods half-green and half-withered; these also stood apart. **12** Others brought rods two-thirds green and one-third withered; these also stood apart. **13** Others returned rods two-thirds withered and one-third green; these also stood apart. **14** Others returned rods nearly all green — only the very tip withered; these stood apart. **15** The rods of still others were completely green; these stood apart, and the angel greatly rejoiced over them, and the shepherd also rejoiced.

---

### Translator's Note
Similitude 8 opens with one of Hermas's most elaborate sorting visions. The willow tree (itea) will be identified in ch. 79 as the Law/Son of God who sustains all people. The ten gradations of branch condition (vv. 6-15) form a precise spiritual taxonomy that the angel will interpret across the following chapters. SOPHIA follows LOGOS's formal taxonomy while incorporating PNEUMA's descriptive clarity in verse 2.
